newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil direct investment up 51.3 pct in Q1 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil direct investment up 51.3 pct in Q1 - paper.

text.p: Net foreign direct investment into Brazil in the first quarter of the year reached $1.769 billion, 51.3 percent over the same period of 1996, Gazeta Mercantil financial newspaper said.
This figure does not consider the $929 million HSBC Holdings Plc brought in for the takeover of selected assets and obligations of private bank Banco Bamerindus, the paper said.
Foreign investment into Brazilian stock exchanges jumped to $3.276 billion from $1.630 billion in the period, a rise of 101 percent, it added.
Central Bank International Affairs director Gustavo Franco told the newspaper overall foreign investment in the first quarter virtually doubled compared with the same period of last year.
He also said the capital account and the quality of the investment have been improving.
"It is becoming more clear that the quality of the investment is improving, reducing anxiety over the trade deficit," Franco was quoted as saying.
Most pessimistic market analysts predict Brazil's trade deficit is likely to reach $15 billion this year, well above last year's record $5.5 billion trade gap, Gazeta said.
Franco also told the newspaper the widening trade deficit may raise concern but is not "catastrophic" as it can be easily financed.

"It is difficult to have any projection about the current account deficit. What is important is that we have a comfortable level of foreign capital coming in, especially direct investment," he was quoted as saying.
